Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0, 10.0.3-r0, 10.0.4-r0, 10.0.5-r0, 10.0.6-r0, 10.0.7-r0, 10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold: every build ships System.Private.CoreLib.dll at its own .NET version, in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet10-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap, and in the runtime pack, NativeAOT pack and runtime archives held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap (seven copies per build and architecture); no copy from another .NET version is present. That version is 10.0.2 to 10.0.10 in the first nine builds and 10.0.13 or later from 10.0.13-r0 on. The range ends at 10.0.13-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-96233 (GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9) is a .NET denial of service issue in System.Runtime: parsing a DateTime that contains Hebrew numbers can read outside the expected stack bounds and terminate the process. Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected and the .NET 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/481, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135708, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside the nupkg and other zip archives they hold: every implementation copy of System.Private.CoreLib.dll, which holds the DateTime parsing code, carries the build's own .NET version: in the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework of dotnet8-runtime and of the .NET SDK held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap, and in that version's runtime pack and NativeAOT compiler pack held by dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap. In the x86_64 dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap package, the shared-framework copy reports product version 8.0.31 in 8.0.31-r0 and 8.0.32 in 8.0.32-r0. So the copies are 8.0.23 to 8.0.31 in the first seven builds and 8.0.32 or later from 8.0.32-r0 on. The range ends at 8.0.32-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-96233 (GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9) is a .NET denial of service issue in System.Runtime: DateTime parsing of Hebrew numbers can read outside expected stack bounds and terminate the process. Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected platforms and the .NET 10.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12 and fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/481, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135708, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). The fix, https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/commit/d9b2f326d2829d4e741404a24b6fce979733f20e ('Fix DateTime parsing with Hebrew numbers'), bounds the DateTime parser's three-number buffer in System.Private.CoreLib and adds a ThrowNumberBufferOverflow guard; it is in the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.113 source tag, from which the 10.0.13 runtime is built, and in later tags, and not in v10.0.112. DHI dotnet-runtime-10 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's prebuilt .NET Runtime for Linux, checked at build time against the SHA-512 hash Microsoft publishes in https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/releases.json, and each build's version starts with the .NET runtime version it carries. We unpacked every package built from this source that the DHI Debian repository published as of 2026-11-27, builds 10.0.9-0, 10.0.10-0, 10.0.11-0, 10.0.12-0, 10.0.13-0, 10.0.14-0, 10.0.15-0 and 10.0.15-1, the dotnet-runtime-10 packages for amd64 and arm64 and the dotnet-runtime-10-oci-config packages, after checking each against its index checksum (no debug-symbol packages are published). Each dotnet-runtime-10 package holds the dotnet host, one hostfxr and one shared framework, /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version>: together 172 managed .NET assemblies and 16 dynamically linked ELF programs and libraries, all of which link the system C library (libc.so.6), plus license, JSON, version and changelog text files, and no native Windows executables, Mach-O files, static archives or zip or nupkg archives. The oci-config packages hold one configuration file and a changelog, and no .NET assemblies or native code. Each build has one System.Private.CoreLib.dll, in the shared framework. Its product version names the .NET version and the dotnet/dotnet source tag commit it was built from: 10.0.9 to 10.0.12 (tags v10.0.109 to v10.0.112) in builds 10.0.9-0 to 10.0.12-0, and 10.0.13 in 10.0.13-0, 10.0.14 in 10.0.14-0 and 10.0.15 (tags v10.0.113 to v10.0.115) in 10.0.15-0 and 10.0.15-1, the same on both architectures. The ThrowNumberBufferOverflow name is absent from System.Private.CoreLib.dll in 10.0.9-0 to 10.0.12-0 and present from 10.0.13-0 on, on both architectures; the DateTimeRawInfo type name, searched the same way, is found in every build. The range ends at 10.0.13-0, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-96233 (GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9) is a .NET denial of service issue in System.Runtime: parsing a DateTime that contains Hebrew numbers can read outside the expected stack bounds and terminate the process. Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected and the .NET 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/481, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135708. The .NET 8 fix is dotnet/runtime commit 2aa2ba850487fe41bfe1550a7252aa3b6461db96 on release/8.0 (Fix DateTime parsing with Hebrew characters), which bounds the number buffer in DateTimeParse.cs in System.Private.CoreLib and throws through a new ThrowNumberBufferOverflow helper when it is full; it is in the v8.0.32, v8.0.33 and v8.0.34 tags and not in v8.0.31: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/2aa2ba850487fe41bfe1550a7252aa3b6461db96. DHI dotnet-runtime-8 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET 8 runtime tarball for Linux under /usr/lib/dotnet, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. The DHI Debian repository had published these builds of this source by 2026-11-27, each for amd64 and arm64: 8.0.28-0, 8.0.29-0, 8.0.30-0, 8.0.31-0, 8.0.32-0, 8.0.33-0, 8.0.34-0 and 8.0.34-1 (the dotnet-runtime-8 and dotnet-runtime-8-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published). We read the file manifest of every one of these packages: each dotnet-runtime-8 build holds one .NET shared framework, Microsoft.NETCore.App, at the build's own runtime version (8.0.28 to 8.0.34; both 8.0.34 builds carry 8.0.34), and no other copy of the runtime; the -oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Unpacking every dotnet-runtime-8 package (checked against its index checksum) found the same contents in each build: 15 ELF files, all dynamically linked against the system C library, and 168 managed .NET assemblies (PE files with a CLR header), with no native Windows PE, Mach-O or static archive files. The DateTime parsing code is in System.Private.CoreLib.dll, and each build carries one copy, in the shared framework. libcoreclr.so and System.Private.CoreLib.dll record the dotnet/runtime commit they were built from: the v8.0.31 tag commit (1219a42) in 8.0.31-0 and the v8.0.32 tag commit (b9a49e4) in 8.0.32-0, on both architectures (libcoreclr.so version 8.0.3126.42015 and 8.0.3226.50405); the 8.0.33-0 build carries the v8.0.33 tag commit and the 8.0.34 builds the v8.0.34 tag commit. In 8.0.32-0 and 8.0.33-0 every file under /usr/lib/dotnet has the same MD5 as Microsoft's dotnet-runtime 8.0.32 and 8.0.33 tarballs for the same architecture (the tarballs checked against the SHA-512 in Microsoft's releases.json). The helper name ThrowNumberBufferOverflow that the fix adds is in the metadata of System.Private.CoreLib.dll in 8.0.32-0 (arm64) and 8.0.33-0 (amd64) and absent from 8.0.31-0 (amd64), where the same search finds the DateTimeRawInfo type. The range ends at 8.0.32-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

Microsoft lists Windows, Linux and macOS as affected and the .NET 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-x64 and linux-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31 and fixed in 8.0.32: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-87vj-4hqv-22p9, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/481, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135708. The .NET 8 fix is dotnet/runtime commit 2aa2ba850487fe41bfe1550a7252aa3b6461db96 on release/8.0 (Fix DateTime parsing with Hebrew characters), which bounds the number buffer in DateTimeParse.cs in System.Private.CoreLib and throws through a new ThrowNumberBufferOverflow helper when it is full; it is in the v8.0.32, v8.0.33 and v8.0.34 tags and not in v8.0.31: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/commit/2aa2ba850487fe41bfe1550a7252aa3b6461db96. DHI dotnet-runtime-8 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET 8 runtime tarball for Linux under /usr/lib/dotnet, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. The DHI Debian repository had published these builds of this source by 2026-11-27, each for amd64 and arm64: 8.0.28-0, 8.0.29-0, 8.0.30-0, 8.0.31-0, 8.0.32-0, 8.0.33-0, 8.0.34-0 and 8.0.34-1 (the dotnet-runtime-8 and dotnet-runtime-8-oci-config packages; no debug-symbol packages are published). We read the file manifest of every one of these packages: each dotnet-runtime-8 build holds one .NET shared framework, Microsoft.NETCore.App, at the build's own runtime version (8.0.28 to 8.0.34; both 8.0.34 builds carry 8.0.34), and no other copy of the runtime; the -oci-config packages hold only an image configuration YAML file and a changelog. Unpacking every dotnet-runtime-8 package (checked against its index checksum) found the same contents in each build: 15 ELF files, all dynamically linked against the system C library, and 168 managed .NET assemblies (PE files with a CLR header), with no native Windows PE, Mach-O or static archive files. The DateTime parsing code is in System.Private.CoreLib.dll, and each build carries one copy, in the shared framework. libcoreclr.so and System.Private.CoreLib.dll record the dotnet/runtime commit they were built from: the v8.0.31 tag commit (1219a42) in 8.0.31-0 and the v8.0.32 tag commit (b9a49e4) in 8.0.32-0, on both architectures (libcoreclr.so version 8.0.3126.42015 and 8.0.3226.50405); the 8.0.33-0 build carries the v8.0.33 tag commit and the 8.0.34 builds the v8.0.34 tag commit. In 8.0.32-0 and 8.0.33-0 every file under /usr/lib/dotnet has the same MD5 as Microsoft's dotnet-runtime 8.0.32 and 8.0.33 tarballs for the same architecture (the tarballs checked against the SHA-512 in Microsoft's releases.json). The helper name ThrowNumberBufferOverflow that the fix adds is in the metadata of System.Private.CoreLib.dll in 8.0.32-0 (arm64) and 8.0.33-0 (amd64) and absent from 8.0.31-0 (amd64), where the same search finds the DateTimeRawInfo type. The range ends at 8.0.32-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.
